30.text: RBI was nationalised in 1949.
RBI was nationalised on January 1, 1949.
RBI was nationalised through the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
The Banking Regulation Act was enacted in 1949.
SBI was established in 1955.
SBI was established on July 1, 1955.
SBI was established by taking over the Imperial Bank of India.
SBI was established under the State Bank of India Act, 1955.
LIC was nationalised in 1956.
LIC was nationalised on September 1, 1956.
LIC was nationalised through the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956.
LIC nationalisation merged over 240 private insurers and societies.
The SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act was passed in 1959.
The SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act brought 8 princely state-associated banks under SBI ownership.
The 8 princely state-associated banks later became known as SBI Associate Banks.
14 major commercial banks were nationalised in 1969.
The 14 major commercial banks were nationalised on July 19, 1969.
The 14 major commercial banks had deposits of at least ₹50 crore when they were nationalised.
The 14 major commercial banks were nationalised under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1969.
Regional Rural Banks were established in 1975.
Regional Rural Banks were established on October 2, 1975.
Regional Rural Banks were established following the recommendations of the Narasimham Working Group.
Prathama Bank was the first Regional Rural Bank.
Six more commercial banks were nationalised in 1980.
The six more commercial banks were nationalised on April 15, 1980.
The six more commercial banks had deposits of at least ₹200 crore when they were nationalised.
Andhra Bank was one of the six commercial banks nationalised in 1980.
Corporation Bank was one of the six commercial banks nationalised in 1980.
New Bank of India was one of the six commercial banks nationalised in 1980.
Oriental Bank of Commerce was one of the six commercial banks nationalised in 1980.
Punjab & Sind Bank was one of the six commercial banks nationalised in 1980.
Vijaya Bank was one of the six commercial banks nationalised in 1980.
NABARD was established in 1982.
NABARD was established on July 12, 1982.
NABARD was established under the recommendations of the B. Sivaraman Committee.
NABARD was established through the NABARD Act, 1981.
EXIM Bank was set up in 1982.
SIDBI was established in 1990.
SIDBI was established on April 2, 1990.
SIDBI is the principal financial institution for the promotion and financing of MSMEs.
The Narasimham Committee I report was submitted in 1991.
The Narasimham Committee I report kicked off economic liberalisation.
The Narasimham Committee I report led to the entry of private banks.
The Narasimham Committee I report led to the deregulation of interest rates.
New Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank in 1993.
The merger of New Bank of India into Punjab National Bank was the first major PSB merger.
New Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank because of financial distress.
The 1993 merger reduced the number of nationalised banks from 20 to 19.
Five SBI associate banks merged into the State Bank of India in 2017.
SBBJ merged into the State Bank of India in 2017.
SBH merged into the State Bank of India in 2017.
SBM merged into the State Bank of India in 2017.
SBP merged into the State Bank of India in 2017.
SBT merged into the State Bank of India in 2017.
Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged into the State Bank of India in 2017.
Dena Bank merged into Bank of Baroda in 2019.
Vijaya Bank merged into Bank of Baroda in 2019.
The Bank of Baroda consolidation took effect on April 1, 2019.
Ten Public Sector Banks merged into four anchor banks in 2020.
The mega PSB consolidation took effect on April 1, 2020.
Oriental Bank of Commerce merged into Punjab National Bank in 2020.
United Bank of India merged into Punjab National Bank in 2020.
Syndicate Bank merged into Canara Bank in 2020.
Andhra Bank merged into Union Bank of India in 2020.
Corporation Bank merged into Union Bank of India in 2020.
Allahabad Bank merged into Indian Bank in 2020.
The 2020 PSB consolidation reduced the number of Public Sector Banks in India to 12.
The Central Government approved a Strategic Disinvestment and Modernisation Policy framework in 2021 and later.
The policy framework provides for the potential privatisation of selected public sector lenders.
The policy framework provides for the potential stake reduction of selected public sector lenders.
The policy framework retains a minimum government presence in strategic sectors.
The policy framework prioritises digital banking units.
The policy framework prioritises PSB governance reforms.
